description: Twelve centered, rotationally symmetric assemblies of flat vector primitives -- triangles, squares, and occasionally a large filled disc -- floating on a near-black charcoal square with generous margin. Each token follows the same grammar: a dominant central body (a big triangle, a two-triangle six-point star, a diamond, a rosette of overlapping polygons, or a solid circle with a dark 'eye' inset) ringed by a regular angular array of smaller satellites of the same primitive, at 3-, 5-, 6-, 8- or 10-fold intervals. The palette is strictly one warm hue -- brass/ochre gold -- worked entirely by alpha and value, so overlapping shapes stack into olive, umber and near-black browns; there is no second hue anywhere and no gradient other than what transparency produces. Density and luminance vary widely across the twelve: 9011 is nearly empty (three small triangles), 9190 and 10980 carry fifteen-plus overlapping members, and 9369/9906/10085 are dominated by a single disc covering most of the frame, while 10622, 10801 and 10980 sit almost entirely in the dark brown end of the ramp. What the twelve share is the centered radial grammar, the single hue, the transparency stacking and the dark ground; what separates them is primitive family (triangle / square / circle), symmetry order, overall brightness, and whether a solid disc anchors the composition or the field stays open. Across the three conditions the object contracts and dims under stress (9190's cluster shrinks to roughly 60% and loses its bright core; 9369's gold disc vanishes entirely, leaving a small dark knot; 9548's eight-square ring collapses to three scattered squares) and expands, re-brightens and gains thin bright stroke-only outlines under recovery (9011 acquires a large gold-outlined triangle absent in neutral; 9548 gains a bright gold zigzag ring; 9369's disc returns larger with a brighter rosette).
seenAt120: Silhouette and gross density survive cleanly: disc, starburst, square-ring, diamond and triangle-cluster are all separable at browse size, and the bright members (9906, 10085, 10443, 9369, 9190, 9727) still read as distinct objects. What is lost is internal overlap structure -- the layered polygon rosette inside 9369 flattens to a dark blob and the 'eye' detail disappears. The dark-ramp tokens are the weak end: 10622, 10801 and 10980 drop to low-contrast brown smudges against the near-black ground, with 10801 barely separating from the field at all, and 10264/10622/10801 read as three variations of the same dim triangle cluster rather than three different works.
